editorial.thesis: A hospitality-and-food-and-drink city of about 1.5 million. Its retail is heavy on cafés, tea & coffee and desserts, sweets & ice cream, and thin on coaching & training and pharmacy & health retail — and 25% of residents live in zones with under 60% of the city's average retail depth.
takeaways: Branded retail is ahead of Faridabad. 52.82 chain outlets per lakh residents against 11.28 in Faridabad; 45 of the 51 national brands we track are present, led by Domino's 89, Apollo Pharmacy 66, Subway 54.

The mapped economy leans to hotels & stays. Shares of all mapped places: hotels & stays 6.7% (Faridabad 3.0%); food & beverage 9.0% (Faridabad 6.0%); education 6.9% (Faridabad 11.5%); banks & finance 7.1% (Faridabad 8.3%). Raw counts would mislead because Faridabad is mapped less completely (14,695 places against 35,365), so we compare mix, not counts.

Supply and demand are misaligned. 5 zones hold 25% of residents with under 60% of the city's average retail depth. Palam Vihar Gurgaon alone has about 110,000 residents and 87 mapped food & drink places.
Retail is less concentrated than in Faridabad. 44% of commercial places sit in the busiest tenth of the city (Faridabad 44%). The largest cores are Gurgaon (7,743 places) and DLF QE (4,474).

The widest brand gaps against Faridabad. Lifestyle 1 outlets vs 3; More 4 outlets vs 5; Biryani By Kilo 1 outlets vs 1. These are leads to check against live listings, not verdicts: a brand may trade under another name or have opened since the map was updated.

numbers.title: The city in eight numbers
numbers.deck: A 8 km circle around the centre, processed with the same rules as Faridabad, so every comparison is like for like. Where raw counts would mislead — because a bigger city is mapped more completely — we compare shares and mix instead.

map.title: Where people live, where shops are
map.deck: Switch layers. The amber “gap” layer is the one to study: it marks places with many residents but little retail around them. Hover any hexagon (about 0.1 km²) for its numbers; click a zone on the right to isolate it.

captions.residents: Where people live. Gurgaon and DLF QE are the largest zones by residents (451,000 and 217,000). Modelled residents per square kilometre.
captions.supply: Where the shops are. The busiest tenth of cells hold 44% of all commercial places, and Gurgaon alone lists 7,743.
captions.chains: Where the brands are. Gurgaon holds 178 of the 771 tracked chain outlets, and DLF QE adds 142.
captions.education: Where the campuses are. Gurgaon and DLF QE lead on education places (727 and 234, with 261 and 79 coaching centres) — a daytime youth market that residents alone do not show.
captions.gap: The gap. Amber: many residents nearby, little retail. Blue: far more retail than local residents explain — the commercial cores that draw people in. The deepest amber sits in Palam Vihar Gurgaon and Industrial Complex Dundahera. The blue cores include Gurgaon.

zones.title: Zone by zone, by PIN code
zones.deck: Each zone is a postal-code area. Residents are modelled counts; places are mapped businesses and services. “Retail depth” is places per 10,000 residents — the tick marks the city average. Click a row to see it on the map.

mix.title: What the retail layer is made of
mix.deck: Raw counts per resident would favour whichever city is mapped more completely (14,695 places in Faridabad against 35,365 here). So this compares each category's share of all mapped places. 100 means the same share as Faridabad; below 100 is thinner, above is stronger.
mix.note: Against Faridabad, Gurugram's mapped places over-index on hotels & stays (6.7% vs 3.0%), food & beverage (9.0% vs 6.0%), desserts & sweets (0.6% vs 0.4%) and under-index on education (6.9% vs 11.5%), banks & finance (7.1% vs 8.3%), malls & department stores (0.7% vs 0.8%).

chains.title: Who is mapped here, and who is not
chains.deck: 771 outlets of 45 tracked national brands within 8 km — 52.82 per lakh residents against Faridabad's 11.28 (214 outlets of 37 brands). Filled names have at least one mapped outlet (count shown); dashed names have none.
chains.note: Read dashed names as leads, not verdicts. “No mapped outlet” can mean a brand trades under a different listed name, or has opened since the map was updated. The widest gaps against Faridabad are Lifestyle (1 vs 3); More (4 vs 5); Biryani By Kilo (1 vs 1). Premium reports check every lead against live listings.

formats.title: Which formats have room
formats.deck: 9 formats, thinnest first. The index is the format's share of all mapped places relative to Faridabad's, so low means thin by Faridabad's standard. “Where to look” ranks zones with at least 40,000 residents by residents per mapped outlet — a first-pass screen for where one more outlet would face the least local competition.

people.title: Who the customers are
people.deck: Age mix inside the 8 km circle, from Meta's age rasters (modelled, not a census).
people.note: Gurugram's age mix against Faridabad: children (0–14) 27.0% vs 27.6%, 15–24 19.3% vs 20.4%, working age 46.4% vs 45.7%, 60+ 7.4% vs 6.3%. Under-25s are 46% of residents.

restaurants.read: Restaurants & fast food are 6.0% of mapped places against 4.4% in Faridabad — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Domino's 89 (Faridabad 36), Subway 54 (Faridabad 10), Pizza Hut 49 (Faridabad 11), KFC 40 (Faridabad 7). No mapped outlet in either city: Faasos.
restaurants.watch: Independent eateries are numerous and unevenly mapped. Treat the index as a screen and confirm competitor density street by street.

cafes.read: Cafés, tea & coffee are 2.5% of mapped places against 1.6% in Faridabad — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Café Coffee Day 50 (Faridabad 6), Starbucks 31 (Faridabad 2), Chaayos 24 (Faridabad 3), Blue Tokai 19 (Faridabad 3).
cafes.watch: Chai stalls and independent cafés are under-mapped. A café concept here competes on price and habit as much as on novelty.

desserts.read: Desserts, sweets & ice cream are 0.6% of mapped places against 0.4% in Faridabad — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Baskin Robbins 18 (Faridabad 4), Theobroma 5 (Faridabad 1), Naturals 2 (Faridabad 0), Havmor 1 (Faridabad 0). No mapped outlet in either city: Cream Stone.
desserts.watch: Traditional sweet shops are the real benchmark and sit outside most chain lists.

grocery.read: Grocery & daily needs are 1.6% of mapped places against 1.4% in Faridabad — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Reliance Smart / Fresh 15 (Faridabad 6), Spencer's 11 (Faridabad 2), Vishal Mega Mart 8 (Faridabad 2), More 4 (Faridabad 5). No mapped outlet in either city: Star Bazaar.
grocery.watch: Neighbourhood kirana stores are the real incumbents and the least completely mapped outlets, so any gap is overstated. Test a site against local store density before acting.

pharmacy.read: Pharmacy & health retail are 1.2% of mapped places against 1.5% in Faridabad — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Apollo Pharmacy 66 (Faridabad 16), MedPlus 1 (Faridabad 0). No mapped outlet in either city: Wellness Forever, Frank Ross.
pharmacy.watch: Independent chemists are dense and lightly mapped. Hospital and clinic clusters are the natural anchors.

apparel.read: Apparel, footwear & jewellery are 4.1% of mapped places against 4.0% in Faridabad, so the mix is level. Mapped chain outlets: Bata 28 (Faridabad 20), Raymond 18 (Faridabad 9), Reliance Trends 16 (Faridabad 3), Titan 15 (Faridabad 3). No mapped outlet in either city: Max Fashion.
apparel.watch: Established multi-brand traders and local bazaars sit behind these numbers; new entrants compete with them as well as with chains.

banking.read: Banks & ATMs are 7.1% of mapped places against 8.3% in Faridabad — below its share.
banking.watch: This category includes insurance and agency offices, so it overstates branch banking. Use it as a signal of commercial activity, not a branch count.

coaching.read: Coaching & training are 2.1% of mapped places against 3.1% in Faridabad — below its share.
coaching.watch: Coaching demand follows the exam calendar. Formats that depend on it should be tested across the academic year.

fitness.read: Fitness & wellness are 5.1% of mapped places against 4.4% in Faridabad — above its share.
fitness.watch: Gym listings change often and are inconsistently categorised; verify before drawing conclusions.
